title: Create and configure an Operator
summary: Build Operator with strategies and construction knobs, add_strategy / set_parameter for shared parameter names, and is_ready. False from is_ready before a backtest fills buffers can be normal. Frequency routing and signal-number meanings are other cards.
narrative:
Create an Operator with qt.Operator(...). You may pass strategies (id string, list, or instances) plus construction knobs such as signal_type. Add more with add_strategy / add_strategies. Use set_parameter(stg_id, pars={parameter_name: value, ...}) to set one shared parameter set for a strategy by parameter name—not a per-share code map.

is_ready() (or op.ready) checks whether the Operator can emit signals. Before a backtest or live run fills the share pool, data buffers, and timing tables, False is normal; those pieces are filled by the run pipeline. Pass tell_me_why=True to print the missing pieces.

This card does not explain where run timing belongs versus qt.run, and it does not define what PT / PS / VS numbers mean. Mixing several strategies inside a Group is the blender card.
python_code:
import qteasy as qt
op = qt.Operator(signal_type='pt')
op.add_strategy('dma')
op.set_parameter('dma', pars={'short_period': 5, 'long_period': 20})
print(op.is_ready(tell_me_why=True))
risk_notes: Ask does not call qt.run. A False is_ready before buffers exist is often expected, not a broken Operator.
